judgment.scope_reason: Asserted by PAINT at PTN000916590 and true of every member: the ALDH fold with an intact catalytic cysteine and glutamate is present throughout, and no member is known to have lost it. Uninformative on its own, which is why individual gene reviews should also carry the specific activity they can support (the exaC review marks this term TOO_GENERAL beside its accepted GO:0140087), but it is not wrong at family level. The Pseudomonas putida KT2440 member reviews aldB-I, aldB-II and pedI mark the InterPro2GO row MARK_AS_OVER_ANNOTATED, but their stated reasons are that the term is uninformative beside a specific aldehyde dehydrogenase term, not that the chemistry is missing. That agrees with this assessment, and on re-review those rows would be better recorded as TOO_GENERAL. They are not member exceptions, because the term does hold for those proteins.
